item.title: TensorFlow Extended (TFX)
item.description:
To create a TFX pipeline:

  1. Ensure your Provider supports TFX by specifying the TFX image in spec.frameworks[].
  2. Create a Pipeline resource, specifying:
  • the tfx framework in spec.framework.name. This needs to match the name specified in the Provider.
  • the fully qualified name of the Python function creating TFX pipeline components under spec.framework.parameters[].components.
  • any required beam arguments under spec.framework.parameters[].beamArgs.
Note

We aim to track current Python versions and follow Python’s release lifecycle, dropping each version once it reaches end of life. We advise using the newest version the compilers support (currently 3.12).

item.title: Kubeflow Pipelines SDK (KFP SDK)
item.description:
To create a KFP SDK pipeline:

  • Ensure your Provider supports KFP SDK by specifying the KFP SDK image in spec.frameworks[].
  • Create a Pipeline resource, specifying:
    • the kfpsdk framework in spec.framework.name. This needs to match the name specified in the Provider.
    • the fully qualified name of the Python function that creates a KFP SDK pipeline under spec.framework.parameters[].pipeline.
Note

We aim to track current Python versions and follow Python’s release lifecycle, dropping each version once it reaches end of life. We advise using the newest version the compilers support (currently 3.12).

item.title: Adding a custom pipeline framework
item.description:
If your desired framework is not natively supported by the KFP Operator, you can provide a custom Docker image that contains the necessary dependencies and code to compile pipelines using your desired framework.

This image should be pushed to a container registry that the KFP Operator deployment has access to. e.g. ghcr.io/kfp-operator/kfp-operator-custom-compiler:version-tag

Follow these steps to build the image and configure your installation of the KFP Operator:

  1. Follow the steps in the compilers README to build your custom Docker image, ensuring it conforms to the correct structure. Examples of the structure can be found in the code for the natively supported frameworks. This image will be called by a set of Argo Workflows, with these parameters.
  2. Publish the Docker image to a repository accessible via the KFP Operator deployment.
  3. Update your Provider resource to support your custom framework by specifying your framework name and image in spec.frameworks[].
  4. To then use the custom framework in a Pipeline resource, simply configure spec.framework to take the same name as the framework set in the Provider resource, and any additional parameters that your framework requires.
